    <h2 id="what-is-medusa">1. What is MEDUSA?</h2>

    <p><strong>MEDUSA</strong> is a comprehensive Static Application Security Testing (SAST) tool built for the AI
        era. Created by Pantheon Security, it combines traditional code security scanning with cutting-edge AI agent
        security rules.</p>

    <p>Unlike legacy SAST tools that focus solely on code vulnerabilities, MEDUSA recognizes that modern development
        involves AI assistants, LLM integrations, and agentic workflows - each introducing new attack vectors that
        traditional scanners miss.</p>

    <h3>Key Capabilities</h3>

    <div class="feature-grid">
        <div class="feature-card">
            <i class="fas fa-search"></i>
            <h4>74 Scanners</h4>
            <p>Covers all major languages with intelligent selection</p>
        </div>
        <div class="feature-card">
            <i class="fas fa-robot"></i>
            <h4>180+ AI Rules</h4>
            <p>Prompt injection, tool poisoning, RAG attacks</p>
        </div>
        <div class="feature-card">
            <i class="fas fa-filter"></i>
            <h4>Smart FP Filter</h4>
            <p>40-60% false positive reduction</p>
        </div>
        <div class="feature-card">
            <i class="fas fa-bolt"></i>
            <h4>Parallel Processing</h4>
            <p>10-40x faster than sequential scanning</p>
        </div>
    </div>

    <h3>What Makes MEDUSA Different</h3>

    <table>

    <h2 id="installation">2. Installation & Quick Start</h2>

    <h3>System Requirements</h3>
    <ul>
        <li>Python 3.8 or higher</li>
        <li>Windows, macOS, or Linux</li>
        <li>2GB RAM minimum (4GB recommended)</li>
    </ul>

    <h3>Installation</h3>

    <h4>macOS/Linux (Recommended - Virtual Environment)</h4>
    <pre><code># Create and activate virtual environment

python3 -m venv medusa-env source medusa-env/bin/activate

Install MEDUSA

pip install medusa-security

Verify installation

medusa –version

    <h4>Windows</h4>
    <pre><code># Create and activate virtual environment

py -m venv medusa-env medusa-env\Scripts\activate

Install MEDUSA

pip install medusa-security

Verify installation

medusa –version

    <div class="info-box">
        <strong><i class="fas fa-lightbulb"></i> Tip:</strong> For Windows, if the <code>medusa</code> command is
        not found, use <code>py -m medusa</code> instead.
    </div>

    <h3>5-Minute Setup</h3>

    <pre><code># 1. Initialize in your project

cd your-project medusa init

2. Install security tools (auto-detected for your platform)

medusa install –all

3. Run your first scan

medusa scan .

    <h3>Example Output</h3>

    <h3>Intelligent False Positive Reduction</h3>

    <p>MEDUSA's FP filter uses context-aware analysis to reduce noise by 40-60%:</p>

    <ul>
        <li><strong>Security wrapper detection:</strong> Recognizes SecureString, EncryptedCredential patterns</li>
        <li><strong>Docstring/comment exclusion:</strong> Ignores security-related documentation</li>
        <li><strong>Context-aware class analysis:</strong> Understands if code is in test files</li>
        <li><strong>Test/mock file identification:</strong> Reduces alerts for test fixtures</li>
        <li><strong>Known-safe pattern database:</strong> Curated list of false positive patterns</li>
    </ul>

    <h3>CVE Detection</h3>

    <p>MEDUSA actively detects known critical CVEs:</p>

    <div class="warning-box">
        <strong><i class="fas fa-exclamation-triangle"></i> CVE-2025-55182 "React2Shell":</strong> CVSS 10.0 RCE
        vulnerability affecting React Server Components (19.0.0-19.2.0) and Next.js App Router (15.0.0-15.0.4).
        MEDUSA scans package.json, package-lock.json, yarn.lock, and pnpm-lock.yaml.
    </div>

    <div class="warning-box">
        <strong><i class="fas fa-exclamation-triangle"></i> CVE-2025-6514:</strong> MCP-remote RCE vulnerability
        affecting Model Context Protocol servers. MEDUSA detects vulnerable MCP configurations.
    </div>

    <h3>Report Formats</h3>

    <pre><code># JSON - Machine-readable for CI/CD

medusa scan . –format json

HTML - Beautiful glassmorphism UI with charts

medusa scan . –format html

Markdown - GitHub/wiki friendly

medusa scan . –format markdown

SARIF - GitHub Security tab integration

medusa scan . –format sarif

All formats at once

medusa scan . –format all

    <h2 id="ai-security">4. AI Agent Security (180+ Rules)</h2>

    <p>This is where MEDUSA truly shines. With 180+ specialized rules for AI/LLM security, it's the first SAST tool
        purpose-built for the agentic era.</p>

    <h3>Attack Categories Covered</h3>

    <h4><i class="fas fa-keyboard" style="color: var(--accent-red);"></i> Context & Input Attacks</h4>
    <ul>
        <li>Prompt injection patterns</li>
        <li>Role/persona manipulation</li>
        <li>Hidden instructions in system prompts</li>
        <li>Obfuscation tricks (Base64, Unicode, etc.)</li>
    </ul>

    <h4><i class="fas fa-memory" style="color: var(--accent-orange);"></i> Memory & State Attacks</h4>
    <ul>
        <li>Memory poisoning</li>
        <li>Context manipulation</li>
        <li>Checkpoint tampering</li>
        <li>Cross-session data exposure</li>
    </ul>

    <h4><i class="fas fa-tools" style="color: var(--accent-purple);"></i> Tool & Action Attacks</h4>
    <ul>
        <li>Tool poisoning (CVE-2025-6514)</li>
        <li>Command injection via tools</li>
        <li>Tool name spoofing</li>
        <li>Confused deputy patterns</li>
    </ul>

    <h4><i class="fas fa-sitemap" style="color: var(--accent-cyan);"></i> Workflow & Routing Attacks</h4>
    <ul>
        <li>Router manipulation</li>
        <li>Agent impersonation</li>
        <li>Workflow hijacking</li>
        <li>Delegation abuse</li>
    </ul>

    <h4><i class="fas fa-database" style="color: var(--accent-green);"></i> RAG & Knowledge Attacks</h4>
    <ul>
        <li>Knowledge base poisoning</li>
        <li>Embedding pipeline attacks</li>
        <li>Source confusion</li>
        <li>Retrieval manipulation</li>
    </ul>

    <h3>Supported AI Configuration Files</h3>

    <p>MEDUSA automatically scans these AI-related files:</p>

    <pre><code>.cursorrules          # Cursor AI instructions

CLAUDE.md # Claude Code context .claude/ # Claude configuration directory copilot-instructions.md # GitHub Copilot AGENTS.md # Multi-agent definitions mcp.json # MCP server configs mcp-config.json # MCP configuration *.mcp.ts / *.mcp.py # MCP server code rag.json # RAG configurations knowledge.json # Knowledge base configs memory.json # Agent memory configs

    <h3>Quick AI Security Scan</h3>

    <div class="command-block">
        <code>medusa scan . --ai-only</code>
    </div>

    <h2 id="usage-examples">6. Real-World Usage Examples</h2>

    <h3>Scanning a Python Project</h3>

    <pre><code># Full scan with all reports

medusa scan ./my-python-app –format all

Quick scan (changed files only)

medusa scan ./my-python-app –quick

Scan with 8 workers for faster processing

medusa scan ./my-python-app –workers 8

    <h3>Scanning a Node.js/React Project</h3>

    <pre><code># Check for React2Shell CVE

medusa scan ./my-react-app

Output includes:

🚨 CRITICAL: CVE-2025-55182 React2Shell detected

package.json: react@19.1.0 (vulnerable: 19.0.0-19.2.0)

Fix: Upgrade to react@19.0.1+

    <h3>Scanning AI Agent Configurations</h3>

    <pre><code># Scan only AI-related files

medusa scan . –ai-only

Scan MCP server configuration

medusa scan ./mcp-servers/

    <h3>Fail on High Severity (CI/CD)</h3>

    <pre><code># Fail the build if HIGH or CRITICAL issues found

medusa scan . –fail-on high

Exit codes:

0 = No issues at or above threshold

1 = Issues found at or above threshold

2 = Scan error

    <h2 id="ide-integration">7. IDE Integration</h2>

medusa init –ide claude-code

    <h3>Cursor</h3>

Or all at once

    <div class="success-box">
        <strong><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> Best Practice:</strong> After initializing IDE integration, your
        AI coding assistant will automatically consider security context when generating code, and you can ask it to
        run MEDUSA scans.
    </div>

    <h2 id="cicd">8. CI/CD Integration</h2>

    <h3>GitHub Actions Example</h3>

    <pre><code>name: Security Scan

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs: security: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4

  - name: Set up Python
    uses: actions/setup-python@v5
    with:
      python-version: '3.11'
      
  - name: Install MEDUSA
    run: pip install medusa-security
    
  - name: Initialize MEDUSA
    run: medusa init
    
  - name: Install scanners
    run: medusa install --all --yes
    
  - name: Run security scan
    run: medusa scan . --format sarif --fail-on high
    
  - name: Upload SARIF to GitHub
    uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
    with:
      sarif_file: .medusa/reports/*.sarif</code></pre>

    <h3>GitLab CI Example</h3>

    <pre><code>security_scan:

stage: test image: python:3.11 script: - pip install medusa-security - medusa init - medusa install –all –yes - medusa scan . –format json –fail-on high artifacts: reports: sast: .medusa/reports/*.json

    <h2 id="best-practices">10. Best Practices</h2>

    <h3>When to Run MEDUSA</h3>

    <ul>
        <li><strong>Pre-commit:</strong> Quick scan on changed files</li>
        <li><strong>Pull Request:</strong> Full scan with --fail-on high</li>
        <li><strong>Main branch:</strong> Comprehensive scan with all reports</li>
        <li><strong>Weekly:</strong> Full audit scan with AI-only focus</li>
    </ul>

    <h3>Configuration Best Practices</h3>

    <pre><code># .medusa.yml

version: “1.0”

scan: workers: 6 cache: true fail_on: high

exclude:

  • “node_modules/”
  • “venv/”
  • “*.test.py”
  • “/tests/”

ai_security: enabled: true strict_mode: true

reports: formats: - json - sarif output_dir: “.medusa/reports”

    <h3>Handling Findings</h3>

    <div class="success-box">
        <strong><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> Prioritization Framework:</strong>
        <ol>
            <li><strong>CRITICAL:</strong> Fix immediately - CVEs, prompt injection in production</li>
            <li><strong>HIGH:</strong> Fix before merge - Tool poisoning, RAG vulnerabilities</li>
            <li><strong>MEDIUM:</strong> Plan for next sprint - Configuration issues</li>
            <li><strong>LOW:</strong> Track and address - Style/best practice issues</li>
        </ol>
    </div>

    <h3>Team Workflow</h3>

    <ol>
        <li>Add MEDUSA to CI/CD pipeline</li>
        <li>Set <code>--fail-on high</code> for pull requests</li>
        <li>Review findings in weekly security triage</li>
        <li>Track false positives and update <code>.medusa.yml</code> exclusions</li>
        <li>Run <code>--ai-only</code> scans when updating AI configurations</li>
    </ol>
